issue.title: mongo:latest image is missing mongo binary

repository.name: mongo
repository.description: Docker Official Image packaging for MongoDB

issue.body:
Hi,

as of today we face an issue with the `mongo` command. 

### Steps to reproduce:
* Start a mongodb:
  * `docker run -it --rm --name mongo mongo:latest mongod`
* Execute command `mongo` in the started mongodb
  * `docker exec -it mongo mongo`
This delivers the following error:
`OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed: unable to start container process: exec: "mongo": executable file not found in $PATH: unknown`

With version 5.0 the `mongo` command is working as expected.

### Expected 
`mongo` command is still working

###  Further info
We use a project called testcontainers which starts a mongo:latest and connects with command `mongo`. This fails with the explained behaviour.
Related to this: https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/issues/5768

Best
Michael

body: Thanks for raising the issue! This is not an issue in the image. See the [releases notes ](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/6.0-compatibility/#legacy-mongo-shell-removed) about MongoDB 6 It is not offered as you can see in the image below. We need to update the `MongoDBContainer` to use `mongosh` when image version is 6.0+

issue.title: Add compatibility with MongoDB 6

repository.name: testcontainers-java
repository.description: Testcontainers is a Java library that supports JUnit tests, providing lightweight, throwaway instances of common databases, Selenium web browsers, or anything else that can run in a Docker container.

issue.body:
MongoDB 6 removed `mongo` shell and `mongosh` is recommended.
See [here](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/6.0-compatibility/#legacy-mongo-shell-removed)

Closes #5768

issue.body: Currently, all tests are being run using Mongo DB 4.4. However, Mongo DB 5.0 and 6.0 are already available and we should make sure that we at least support Mongo DB 5.0. If any steps are required to migrate an existing Mongo 4.4 based registry to Mongo 5.0, these steps should be ideally performed automatically or (at least) be documented in the admin guide.
